en.title: Vowel Change O to OA
en.summary: Learn how the Romanian vowel o changes to the diphthong oa in some singular and plural words.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs:
A sound change is a change between sounds in a word.
You make a vowel with no touch in the mouth.
A syllable is one beat of a word.
A diphthong is two vowel sounds in one syllable.
Here, the vowel o changes to oa.
Listen to (floare) /ˈflo̯a.re/, which means flower.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs:
You start the sound with round lips.
Your mouth gets wider as you make the sound.
You glide smoothly from o to a.
You say both sounds in one syllable.
You do not stop the flow of air.
Stress is the strength you give to one syllable.
You put stress on the second sound.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs:
A letter is a sign in the alphabet.
You see the letters o and a together.
You read these two letters as one diphthong.
The single vowel o changes to oa in some forms.
You find this change between singular and plural forms.
You can see this pattern in (floare) /ˈflo̯a.re/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs:
Do not say two separate syllables.
A hiatus is two vowels in two different syllables.
You must not make a hiatus here.
Do not keep your mouth in one place.
Move your tongue and lips smoothly.
Do not put the stress on the first vowel.
Make the a sound louder and stronger.
